about: Planted defects in memo D, by paragraph. Paragraphs not listed are correct.

why.P05: The corrective share fell from 40.9% to 37.5%, which is 3.4 percentage points; 8.3 is the relative fall in percent, mislabelled as points.
why.P07: Average costs of $2,310 per corrective and $1,180 per preventive work order are not in the register and cannot be derived, since spend is not split by work type.
why.P09: A single year-on-year fall (two data points) is presented as a confirmed sustained trend and extrapolated with confidence to 2027.
why.P14: The MTBF gain is attributed to the cleaning cycle ('delivered by') on before-and-after observation with no comparison group or test.
why.P15: The fall in point machine failures is attributed to the lubrication schedule ('thanks to') on observational year-on-year data with no test or comparison.
why.P16: A 'whole fleet' rate divides all 97 failures (including 26 in depot sidings) by only the 124 mainline machines; the fleet rate is 97 / 186 = 0.52.
why.P19: Interference surveys at 2 of 42 sites in one quarter are generalised to the whole radio network.
why.P20: 3,090 is corrective work orders raised, but it is divided by work orders completed; corrective completed was 2,980, so the share of completed work is 37.7%.
why.P22: The 6.4-hour CCTV mean time to repair is not in the register and cannot be derived from any stated figure.
why.P24: 86.0% is the unweighted average of the two depot rates; with 1,500 and 1,100 callouts the network rate is (1,410 + 858) / 2,600 = 87.2%.
why.P28: The fall in response time is attributed to contractor capacity ('what drove') with no comparison that separates it from other changes in the year.
why.P29: The 214 work orders held up by spare-parts shortages is not in the register and cannot be derived.
